items.title: 67251_Chuck Green oral history interview
items.q: Walter Winchell was alive. He was a famous columnist, see, and he wrote about the show, see, and he said something about the dark horse won

ctx.x: Yeah, Buddy Ebsen. They was known tap dancers. Yeah. And there was a fellow -- yeah, and what you call -- yeah, that was about it. You see? Yes, that was it.

And they were playing in shows, like around here -- down there on Broadway, you see? They was in shows. But tap dancing itself, like Bojangles had been discovered by a millionaire, Marty Fawkins (PHONETIC), and he was just handled by Marty Fawkins exclusively. No other entertainer he had but Bojangles Robinson. He was playing at the Palace Theater. And this thing came about that they had all these white dancers, tap dancers, to settle what they called who was the best of the tap dancers, you know, that were…
What I'm trying to get at is what was tap dancing then? Was it very popular? Was a lot of it being done in New York? Was it done on Broadway?
